plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of others' bids or strategies. This is because if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (not your own), so bidding your value ensures you win whenever it's profitable to do so, and never lose when winning would be profitable. Since my value is $9, I will bid exactly $9 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of opponents' strategies. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value only risks overpaying, while bidding lower only risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $9, I should bid exactly $9 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction (where the winner pays the second-highest bid), bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy. This is because if you win, you pay only the second-highest bid regardless of how high you bid above that, so bidding higher than your value risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $34, the optimal action is to bid exactly $34 to maximize expected profit.
